editorial:
Imagine taking a classic old story and mixing it with bright neon lights and a heavy electronic beat. That is exactly what you get here. You follow Dr. Henry Jekyll, a man who thinks every person has a good side and a bad side. He wants to split these two parts apart using chemicals so he can be free from his own guilt. It sounds like a smart plan, but it goes wrong fast. He turns into Mr. Hyde, a cruel monster who does terrible things while Jekyll is not in control. The whole movie feels like a trip back to the eighties with a scary twist, making the old story feel fresh and loud.

You will really love the neon colors and the music, which keep the energy high. The acting is solid, though the plot moves very quickly, so you have to pay attention. Some of the special effects are a bit simple, but that actually adds to the retro charm. If you love weird horror movies that look like a music video, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want those neon colors to really pop, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: By the end, Jekyll realizes he cannot stop Hyde from taking over. The drug has changed him too much, and Hyde is now the dominant personality. In the final scenes, the battle for control ends with Jekyll failing to fix his mistake. He eventually dies because the two halves of his soul cannot live together anymore. It wraps up as a warning that you cannot just throw away the bad parts of yourself without paying a price.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s style and creepy science experiments.
